name: SIL: Thermal Runaway Fault (HEATING, rate-of-rise)
description: Pan temperature exceeds target + 10C during HEATING triggers FAULT_THERMAL_RUNAWAY
legacy_only_reason: Asserts the legacy target + 10 K latch (state_heating_update), which C1 builds compile out: supervisor R2 replaces it (DECISIONS D-RUN). In C1 a reading over target + 10 K with an obeying stage forces the command to 0 without latching (stage 1), and FAULT_THERMAL_RUNAWAY latches when the power stage is not obeying (stage 2a) or the pan keeps rising with no command (stage 2b). The trace also holds 115.0 noise-free for 6.5 s, which the C1 converter path rightly reports as a frozen code (FAULT_ADC_STUCK).

legacy_only_reason: The trace reaches COOLDOWN one 100 ms legacy-SIL update before the heatsink step, with the heatsink at 35 degC (below SAFE_IDLE_TEMP 50). At the firmware's 10 ms control cadence, which the C1 target runs, COOLDOWN ends on its first update (heatsink < 50 -> IDLE) before the step arrives, so the fault is never injected from COOLDOWN. A property of the trace, not of either loop: the replacement runs in both modes.

name: SIL: DEMONSTRATED GAP -- Fan Failure during PAN_DET is not interlocked
description: Fan is off for the entire PAN_DET dwell (power_set_level(5) is active) yet the state machine reaches PREHEAT normally with no fault -- proves check_safety_interlocks() is not called from state_pan_det_update() (only from state_preheat_update() and state_heating_update()). This is a defense-in-depth gap, not a hardware-interlock gap: OCP/OVP/thermal comparators (33ns/9ns/<1ms) remain independent of this software path. NOT part of the required coverage matrix (transition_table.yaml defines no PAN_DET fault row) and intentionally has no hard_assertions -- the current, unsafe behavior is what this scenario documents. Firmware fix (adding check_safety_interlocks() to state_pan_det_update()) is out of scope for this suite; see plan 031 audit note.
finding: SAFETY GAP (demonstrated, not fixed): fan failure injected throughout PAN_DET produces no fault; the machine proceeds to PREHEAT with power_set_level(5) applied and no interlock check. See state_handlers.c state_pan_det_update() vs state_preheat_update()/state_heating_update().
legacy_only_reason: The fan is off for 3 rows (300 ms at the legacy SIL's 100 ms update). PAN_DET ends after 3 updates, 30 ms at the firmware's 10 ms cadence, so on the C1 target the fan is still off when PREHEAT starts and the PREHEAT interlock (correctly) latches FAULT_FAN_FAILURE before row 3. The replacement holds the PAN_DET dwell for 1 s and runs in both modes.
c1_replaced_by: SIL: DEMONSTRATED GAP -- Fan Failure during a 1 s PAN_DET dwell is not interlocked

latency_bound_note: max_latency_ticks = the legacy target + 10 K latch on this trace, (110 - 92) degC / 0.15 K per row = 120 rows, + 2 rows. One bound for both modes: C1 may not be later than legacy here (DECISIONS D-RUN).

latency_bound_note: max_latency_ticks = the legacy target + 10 K latch on this trace, (110 - 80) degC / 0.15 K per row = 200 rows, + 2 rows. One bound for both modes (DECISIONS D-RUN).

name: SIL: Stuck-On Stage with Current Sense Lost (HEATING)
description: Double fault: power stage stuck on and the bus-current sense reading 0 A from tick 85; the pan rises 1.5 K/s from 92 degC. Legacy latches target + 10 K; C1 has no current evidence and latches stage 2b (over target, command 0 for 20 s, still rising).
c1_later_than_legacy_reason: DECISIONS D-RUN trade-off, allowed in runaway-checks.json allowed_later_than_legacy['fault_stuck_on/current_broken']: stage 2b waits rise_hold_s (20 s) so a hot pan placed above target does not trip it; its bound is the worst hazardous double-fault detection there, 35.0 s (350 rows).
latency_bound_note: max_latency_ticks = the legacy target + 10 K latch, 120 rows + 2; max_latency_ticks_c1 = 35.0 s, see c1_later_than_legacy_reason.

name: SIL: Sustained Sensor Rise 20 K/s (HEATING)
description: The reading rises 20 K/s from 92 degC from tick 85 (a sensor-path fault: 1.8 kW cannot heat any modelled pan faster than 3.84 K/s). Legacy trips its 15 K/s per-read check; C1 trips R1 (1 s block means rising > 15 K/s for 5 blocks) before the reading reaches 300 degC.
c1_later_than_legacy_reason: DECISIONS D-RUN: R1 replaces the 15 K/s per-read latch, which false-trips 58 of 75 benign runs (runaway-checks.json legacy_false_trips). R1 needs 5 consecutive 1 s blocks rising > 15 K/s, plus up to 2 blocks of alignment to the onset: 7 s (70 rows). The absolute 300 degC check is unchanged and still evaluates every 10 ms.

name: SIL: Sustained Sensor Rise 20 K/s (PREHEAT)
description: The reading rises 20 K/s from 80 degC from tick 85 during PREHEAT. Legacy trips its 15 K/s per-read check; C1 trips R1 before the reading reaches 300 degC.
c1_later_than_legacy_reason: As for the HEATING case: R1 bound, DECISIONS D-RUN.

name: SIL: C1 Over-Target Reading with an Obeying Stage (HEATING)
description: The reading steps to 115 degC (target + 15 K) at tick 85 and holds for 31 s with an obeying power stage (an h_c drop or a hot pan). C1 supervisor stage 1 holds the command at 0 and nothing latches; legacy latched FAULT_THERMAL_RUNAWAY here.
c1_only_reason: The C1 replacement for the legacy over-target latch (DECISIONS D-RUN: a lowered target, a hot pan or an h_c drop to target + 13 K tripped it falsely). The 31 s hold outlasts the 20 s stage-2b hold.

name: SIL: C1 ADC Frozen Code (IDLE)
description: In IDLE the reading holds 25.0 from tick 16 (last distinct value at tick 15).
c1_only_reason: C1 services the MAX31865 in every state (rtd_service_control_tick, 07h, stale and frozen checks), so its sensor faults are reachable from IDLE. The legacy SIL target does not link the converter service; its RTD checks run only in PREHEAT/HEATING (check_safety_interlocks). RTD_C1_FROZEN_CONVERSIONS (250) identical codes at 50 Hz is 5.0 s = 50 rows from the first held conversion (DECISIONS D-STALE).
